name: fill_clamped_step_table
description: Fills consecutive table entries with a word value that is clamped to zero and to a limit, advancing a fixed-point accumulator by a per-entry increment each step. It hands the remaining entries to another unnamed routine.

name: emit_clamped_span_rows
description: Writes clamped span entries for each remaining row, using a row count read from a table header word. It calls the same stepping routine and finishes the last row with a clamped end value.

name: fill_clamped_table_with_bias
description: Writes clamped table entries while stepping an accumulator by an increment, choosing between two limit values according to the sign of the second increment. It repeats the write loop over the table rows.

name: fill_span_entries_until_end
description: Loops over span entries, writing clamped values and advancing the accumulator, and stops when the end pointer passes its limit. It calls an unnamed routine between passes.

name: write_xorigin_table_entry
description: Stores a clamped x-origin word for the current entry. When a selector global is nonzero it also looks up two words in a table and writes a mask byte for the entry.

name: fill_remaining_clamped_entries
description: Writes the remaining clamped entries of a span table and then one final clamped value at the end of the row. It calls an unnamed routine to finish.

name: emit_clamped_entries_with_mask
description: Writes clamped span entries and, when a selector global is set, a mask byte and a table lookup for each row. It calls three unnamed routines during the pass.

name: blit_table_rows_mode_two
description: When the selector global equals two, it sets a mask byte and programs blitter control and pointer registers for each record in a table. It waits for the blitter to be idle before each transfer.

name: queue_blitter_span_records
description: Walks a table of span records and, for each non-empty span, programs the blitter's control, size and modulo registers after waiting for it to go idle. It then advances a global value for the next span.

name: fill_masked_table_rows
description: Fills a masked table with clamped entries for each row, using an index offset taken from a lookup table. It writes a mask byte and calls unnamed routines to finish each row.

name: program_blitter_span_records
description: Walks span records and computes a word-aligned start address and a bit-shift count for each non-empty span. It programs the blitter registers after waiting for the blitter to be idle.

name: blit_span_table_with_masks
description: Programs blitter control and mask registers from a masked table, setting source and destination pointers for each span. It waits for the blitter to go idle between writes.

name: copy_shifted_lookup_records
description: For each record, looks up two words in a shifted table and writes three packed words into an output table, stepping through the record list. It does not touch hardware registers.

name: scan_back_equal_word_run
description: Walks backward through 32-bit entries while their low words match the first entry's, and returns when a key differs or the start is reached. It has no side effects.

name: scan_back_for_key_change
description: Walks backward over 32-bit entries and returns at the first entry whose low word differs from the one it started with. It has no side effects.

name: stub_return_only
description: An empty stub that only returns to its caller. It is called from several places and does no work.

name: scan_forward_while_word_matches
description: Walks forward over 32-bit entries from the current pointer while the next word matches, then returns. It has no side effects.

name: scan_forward_until_key_mismatch
description: Walks forward through word pairs and stops at the first entry whose key word differs from the one before it. It returns the position reached.

name: stub_return_only
description: An empty stub that only returns to its caller. It is called from one place and does no work.

name: call_selector_and_store_word
description: Sets up a masked selector value and calls an unnamed routine with it. It then conditionally calls another unnamed routine and stores the resulting word into a structure.

name: init_record_from_table_entry
description: Copies several fields from a table entry into a record, storing one value negated, and then returns its input value. If the flag argument is nonzero, it returns an all-ones error value without writing the record.

name: init_record_fields_checked
description: Initializes a record from a table entry with the same field layout as its neighbours, storing a negated step value and several copied words. It returns its input value on success or an all-ones error value when the flag argument is nonzero.

name: init_record_fields_multi_call
description: Initializes a record from a table entry, calling an unnamed routine first and a second time only when a status word bit is set. It stores the copied fields and returns its input or an all-ones error value.

name: return_value_with_high_ones
description: Returns its argument in the low half of a 64-bit result and sets the high half to all ones. It is a small adapter with no other effect.

name: copy_record_and_store_vertices
description: Copies eight words from a source record into globals, then stores two words into three output slots, calling an unnamed routine before each store. It finishes with a cross-product style combination of the coordinate globals.

name: average_word_pairs_with_carry
description: Averages two pairs of 16-bit words using a carry-preserving right shift and stores the results in globals. It then calls two unnamed routines to continue the computation.

name: average_word_pair_tail_call
description: Averages one pair of 16-bit words with carry-preserving shifting, negates one result and combines the globals with it. It then tail-branches into the next routine.

name: compute_weighted_offset_divide
description: Combines global coordinate differences into a weighted sum and divides it by a step value to produce a new offset global. It then calls two unnamed routines and returns.

name: store_routine_result_global
description: Calls an unnamed routine, stores its result in a global variable, and returns the value passed in on the stack unchanged.

name: skip_sentinel_terminated_lists
description: Advances through word lists that end at the sentinel value of minus 32768, skipping several segments, and copies eight words of a record into globals. It calls five unnamed routines during the pass.

name: emit_scaled_point_triplets
description: For each entry, divides two coordinates by ten, looks up signed values in a table (negated for odd quotients), and writes each point as three words. It loops until the count reaches zero.

name: emit_offset_scaled_point_triplets
description: For each entry, subtracts twenty from two coordinates with clamping at zero, divides by ten, and looks up signed table values. It writes each point as three words and loops until the count reaches zero.

name: emit_unoffset_point_triplets
description: For each entry, divides one coordinate by ten, looks up a signed table value (negated for odd quotients), and writes a three-word point record. It loops until the count reaches zero.

name: emit_negated_lookup_point_pairs
description: For each entry, negates a table lookup for one coordinate and looks up another coordinate after subtracting twenty with clamping at zero. It writes three-word records and loops until the count is exhausted.

name: emit_single_lookup_point_triplet
description: Looks up a signed table value for one coordinate divided by ten, negated for odd quotients, and writes it with the other coordinates as a three-word record. It loops until the count reaches zero.

name: emit_negated_point_records_calls
description: Writes three-word point records with one coordinate negated, calling several unnamed routines to transform the points before storing them. It loops until the count reaches zero.

name: walk_sentinel_list_copy_word
description: Walks a list of entries until the sentinel value of minus 32768 is reached, copying a coordinate word from each entry into a global. It returns the stack argument when the list ends.

name: stub_return_stack_argument
description: Returns its stack argument unchanged and does nothing else. It is a tiny stub called from two places.

name: walk_sentinel_list_store_words
description: Walks a list of entries until the sentinel value of minus 32768 is reached, storing coordinate words in globals and calling one unnamed routine per entry. It returns once the list ends.

name: compute_point_delta_pair
description: Returns the difference of the second coordinate pair and the first, packed as two signed words. It has no side effects.

name: compute_point_delta_pair
description: Returns the difference of the second coordinate pair and the first, packed as two signed words. It has no side effects.

name: compute_point_delta_pair
description: Returns the difference of the second coordinate pair and the first, packed as two signed words. It is called from one place.

name: stub_return_only
description: An empty stub that only returns to its caller. It is called from one place and does no work.

name: lookup_word_by_scaled_index
description: Converts an offset into a table index by biasing it, shifting it right by five and clearing the low bit, then returns the word stored at that index. It is a lookup helper with no side effects.

name: call_unnamed_and_return_argument
description: Calls two unnamed routines in sequence and returns its input argument unchanged. It is a pass-through wrapper.

name: compute_projected_vertex_pair
description: Computes a scaled value from a structure field divided by a thousand, then combines coordinate sums with two unnamed arithmetic routines. It stores a clamped result in globals.

name: compute_scaled_offset_difference
description: Computes the difference of two stored coordinates adjusted by a structure field, then scales the result with two unnamed arithmetic routines. The outcome is written to globals.

name: compute_scaled_offset_terms
description: Derives a set of scaled offset terms from structure fields and stores them in globals. It calls two unnamed arithmetic routines along the way.

name: compute_projected_coordinate_terms
description: Computes projected coordinate terms from sums and differences of structure fields, using three unnamed routines for the arithmetic. It stores the results in globals.

name: divide_and_negate_scale_term
description: Stores the negated quotient of two inputs in a global, then computes a clamped scale from two structure fields and calls two unnamed arithmetic routines.

name: scale_field_difference_by_global
description: Computes the difference of two structure fields and scales it by a global multiplier, storing the clamped product in a global. It calls two unnamed arithmetic routines.

name: scale_field_difference_term
description: Computes a field difference from a structure and scales it by a global value, selecting the sign from the difference. It calls two unnamed arithmetic routines.

name: compute_offset_from_scaled_input
description: Scales an input value by a global multiplier, adds an offset from a structure field, and calls two unnamed arithmetic routines to finish the result.

name: store_record_pointer_and_flags
description: Stores a 32-bit pointer argument in one record field, a halved word derived from its input in another field, and a fixed status word in a third. It has no other effect.

name: call_unnamed_and_return_argument
description: Calls an unnamed routine and returns its two input registers unchanged. It is a pass-through wrapper.

name: call_unnamed_and_return_argument
description: Calls an unnamed routine and returns its two input registers unchanged. It is a pass-through wrapper.

name: call_unnamed_and_return_value
description: Calls an unnamed routine and returns its input argument unchanged. It is a pass-through wrapper.

name: fill_block_from_byte_table
description: Calls two unnamed routines, then fills a block of globals by indexing a byte table with an index multiplied by ten. It loops over a fixed count and writes the result to the state globals.

name: silence_audio_channels_and_clear
description: Clears the state of four audio channels and writes silent volume and control values to the sound hardware. It also zeroes several state globals.

name: set_four_state_flags_on
description: Sets four state flag bytes in globals to one. It is a small initialiser with no other effect.

name: build_dma_enable_control_word
description: If a flag byte is set, builds a control word that sets the DMA enable bit plus one bit per channel for channels three down to zero, and stores it in a global. It also sets a second global to all ones.

name: setup_audio_channel_playback
description: Configures audio playback for a channel from a sample table, writing the channel's location and length registers and calling several unnamed routines along the way. It enables the channel's DMA when a flag is set.

name: update_audio_channel_pointer
description: Computes sample pointer and length values from a channel record and writes them into the audio channel registers. It is reached through a gap in the decoded code.

name: update_audio_channel_state
description: Updates a channel record's position and length fields, then writes the audio pointer and length registers for the channel. It calls an unnamed routine to obtain the sample step.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: A two-instruction fragment decoded from a gap in the code. Its body stores one byte and loops over sample bytes, but the static decode is unreliable as a routine.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: A two-instruction fragment decoded from a gap in the code. It stores one byte and enters a sample-byte loop, but the static decode is unreliable as a routine.

name: copy_flagged_table_records
description: If a flag byte in a structure is clear, copies eleven six-byte records within a global table, moving each one forward. Otherwise it does nothing.

name: clear_channel_state_by_index
description: Sets a global to all ones and clears one of four state bytes chosen by a selector argument. It then calls three unnamed routines to finish the update.

name: initialise_channel_record_fields
description: Initialises three fields of a channel structure to fixed starting values and stores an argument in a global. It then calls two unnamed routines to finish.

name: spin_short_delay_loop
description: Counts a loop variable down from five hundred and twelve to zero and returns, giving a short busy-wait delay.

name: countdown_channel_and_trigger
description: Decrements a countdown byte in a channel structure and, when it reaches zero, clears a flag and stores a value. Otherwise it continues through a separate update path.

name: advance_pseudo_random_state
description: Advances a 32-bit shift-register state held in a global once per step of the argument, XORing in a fixed feedback constant when the top bit falls out. It returns a 16-bit value from the state.

name: initialise_serial_port_registers
description: Stores several constant words in globals and writes one fixed value to the serial period hardware register. It is a one-shot initialiser.

name: parse_text_line_into_fields
description: Parses a text line by skipping spaces and stopping at line ends, then scans words and stores them in a table. It calls itself recursively and a trap routine for conversion.

name: load_data_file_via_dos
description: Entry routine that opens the dos library, opens and reads a data file with seek and close, and allocates memory through exec. It also writes the DMA and interrupt enable registers.

name: fill_range_with_nop_pattern
description: Saves a word at a fixed offset, overwrites it with a no-operation instruction pattern, and fills a range of memory with copies of that pattern. It is a code-patching helper.

name: copy_block_backward
description: Copies a block of 32-bit words from one address to another, moving backward from the end of the block. It is a backward memory copy.

name: copy_sixteen_word_palette_table
description: Calls a library routine through a stored vector, then copies sixteen words from a fixed table into a global buffer that holds the colour palette. The background colour register is among those referenced.

name: setup_display_and_sprite_registers
description: Initialises the display registers: bitplane modulos, bitplane control, display window and fetch limits, and sprite positions. It then sets the copper list pointer and the DMA enable value.

name: fill_four_step_word_pairs
description: Writes four pairs of words into a table with a stride of eight, increasing the stored value by eight thousand for each entry.

name: unpack_run_length_bytes
description: Unpacks a run-length encoded byte stream: a zero count ends decoding, a negative count repeats one byte, and a positive count copies a literal run from the input.

name: decode_bit_packed_stream
description: Reads bits from a packed stream one at a time, shifting a data word and looking up words in a table through an index, and writes the results to an output area. It calls one unnamed routine.

name: stub_return_only
description: An empty stub that only returns to its caller. It is reached from a runtime segment and does no work.

name: stub_return_only
description: An empty stub that only returns to its caller. It is reached from a runtime segment and does no work.

name: copy_header_block_to_buffer
description: If the output pointer is non-null, copies sixteen words from a fixed offset in a structure into the output buffer. It is called from the buffer preparation routine.

name: run_endcli_main_program
description: Main entry of the command shell. It calls a library vector, scans a linked list for the largest value in a field, and calls the buffer preparation routine.

name: copy_header_block_to_buffer
description: If the output pointer is non-null, copies sixteen words from a fixed offset in a structure into the output buffer. It is called from the buffer preparation routine.

name: run_loadwb_startup_sequence
description: Program entry for the workbench loader: finds its own task, waits for and reads its startup message, opens the dos library and sets the current directory. It raises an alert on failure.

name: release_resources_and_reply
description: Cleanup routine that finds the current task, restores a saved handler pointer and, if a stored resource exists, closes its file and library, frees its memory and replies to a message. It forbids multitasking while doing so.

name: launch_workbench_tool_with_messages
description: Starts a Workbench tool by looking up its resident tag and launching it, printing a 'Cannot find resident tag' or 'Cannot start tool' message on failure. It opens the icon, intuition and Workbench libraries first.

name: compare_null_terminated_strings
description: Compares two null-terminated strings byte by byte. It returns minus one if the first is less, one if it is greater, and zero when they are equal.

name: search_resident_list_for_tag
description: Walks a list of entries, looking up a resident tag for each through a library call and allocating memory for matches. It returns the first match found or null when the list is exhausted.

name: pad_name_with_separator
description: Copies a short separator string onto a name buffer when its type byte is two, and compares a global string against the buffer. It returns the input byte.

name: write_dot_and_spaces_suffix
description: Writes a dot followed by four spaces into a buffer at a fixed offset, forming a separator suffix.

name: compare_global_string_prefix
description: Compares a global string with a buffer character by character, stopping at the global string's terminator or at the first mismatch. It returns nothing.

name: stub_return_only
description: An empty stub that only returns to its caller and does no work.

name: forward_call_with_stack_pointer
description: Calls another routine, passing its two arguments and a pointer to the caller's stack argument, then returns.

name: format_string_and_measure_length
description: Formats text into a 140-byte stack buffer using the exec formatting library call, then counts characters up to the terminator and returns the length.

name: run_wait_program_main
description: Main entry of the wait command. It calls a library vector, scans a linked list for the largest value in a field, and calls the buffer preparation routine.

name: copy_header_block_to_buffer
description: If the output pointer is non-null, copies sixteen words from a fixed offset in a structure into the output buffer. It is called from the buffer preparation routine.

name: run_disk_validator_main
description: Entry routine of the disk validator program. It is a large body that uses many register-relative accesses and calls several unnamed routines to check the disk.

name: clear_bss_block_at_entry
description: Program entry that calls an unnamed routine and then zeroes a block of memory by writing zero words across a fixed count. It is a start-up memory clear.

name: setup_display_handles_and_fields
description: Stores handles returned by library calls into globals and initialises several fields of a display structure through a series of calls. The demo picture file name is among the referenced text.

name: start_copper_list_from_record
description: Loads a copper list address from a field of a record and passes it to the copper start routine.

name: enable_dma_and_interrupt_channels
description: Calls several unnamed routines with constant channel, size and enable values, and writes the interrupt enable register. It sets up DMA and interrupts for the display and copper.

name: create_process_and_load_segment
description: Allocates a structure, loads the program segment from named files and creates a process for it through library wrappers. It stores the resulting pointers in globals.

name: allocate_and_fill_offset_table
description: Allocates a block of 1152 bytes, stores its address in a global, and fills an array with offsets stepping by 144 for each row. It then calls two unnamed routines.

name: store_constant_and_call
description: Stores the constant 399 into a word field of a global structure and then calls an unnamed routine.

name: call_global_pointer_with_size
description: Loads a pointer from a global table and calls an unnamed routine with it and a fixed size of 1152 bytes.

name: call_two_global_pointers
description: Calls two unnamed routines, passing each the pointer found in a global table entry.

name: call_library_vector_with_word
description: Calls a library function through a base loaded from a global, passing its argument and the low word of the parameter.

name: forward_call_and_return
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns. It adds no logic of its own.

name: lookup_pair_and_call
description: Searches a two-entry table of globals for the second argument, and when it is found calls an unnamed routine with the paired value and stores the parameter.

name: swap_globals_and_call
description: Swaps two global words, then calls an unnamed routine with the swapped values.

name: open_graphics_and_init_fields
description: Opens the graphics and intuition libraries through calls, stores the returned bases in globals, sets a status field of a structure to minus one and initialises several other fields.

name: wait_for_result_then_call
description: Repeatedly calls an unnamed routine until it returns one, two or three, then calls another routine with a global pointer and a fixed offset.

name: load_picture_file_with_status
description: Clears a status global, calls four unnamed routines to load the picture file named in the referenced text, and returns a status value derived from the calls.

name: install_handlers_and_init_state
description: Installs two routine pointers in a global table, writes several constants into globals and clears a short array. It calls seven unnamed routines to set up the state.

name: update_state_tables_branching
description: Large routine that updates several state variables and tables in globals through eleven unnamed calls, branching on the values it reads. The pseudo-code alone does not show a single clear purpose.

name: stub_return_only
description: An empty stub that only returns to its caller and does no work.

name: fill_row_table_when_zero
description: Calls an unnamed routine in a loop and, when it returns zero, fills a row table with the value one hundred and sixty before processing further entries. It calls seven unnamed routines overall.

name: fill_modular_offset_arrays
description: Loops over the count argument and stores two short arrays, each value reduced modulo thirteen and offset by two hundred thirty-two, using results from an unnamed routine.

name: update_offset_arrays_return_first
description: Loops over a count and updates two short arrays by differences and increments, then returns the first updated value.

name: prepare_demo_picture_display
description: Calls several library routines to prepare the display state, then loads the demo picture named in the referenced text and updates display values.

name: build_offset_stepped_entry_list
description: Fills a list of entries in memory with offsets that step by three hundred for one field and by thirty-two thousand for another, copying parameter values into each entry.

name: read_block_from_file
description: Reads a block of 1005 bytes from the open file and, when the read succeeds, copies 32000 bytes into two buffers. It returns minus one when the read fails.

name: load_font_and_sprite_data
description: Reads a block from the file and passes the data to several unnamed routines that set up font and sprite data. The referenced file names are font.dat, land0 and sprites0.dat.

name: read_block_and_dispatch
description: Reads a block of 1005 bytes and, when the read succeeds, passes it to unnamed routines with sizes of 40000 and 64.

name: rotate_and_merge_word_tables
description: Rotates a 16-bit word table by an amount derived from a nibble, then combines the rotated words with a destination buffer using bitwise AND and OR operations.

name: apply_rotated_mask_to_block
description: Processes a block of words using a mask table indexed by an input value, rotating a 32-bit mask on each iteration and writing combined words to the destination.

name: call_and_return_register_pair
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns its two input registers unchanged.

name: combine_masked_table_words
description: Indexes a table with a global value and a register value, then uses the entry to mask and combine words at offsets derived from two registers. It processes a small block on each call.

name: reorder_table_entry_fields
description: Iterates over a table of entries and reorders fields within each one by copying and shifting words and bytes, writing the transformed values back into the same table.

name: shift_byte_buffer_left_three
description: Shifts each byte of a fixed hundred-byte buffer left by three bits in a simple loop.

name: run_nested_index_loops
description: Runs nested loops over a range of indices, calling an unnamed routine for each index that looks up a table with a global value and a register value.

name: call_and_concatenate_registers
description: Calls an unnamed routine and returns a 64-bit value formed from two data registers.

name: store_global_address_pointer
description: Stores the address of a global buffer into a pointer variable and returns.

name: copy_eighty_character_entries
description: Loops over eighty entries, copying character bytes from a source into a destination and clearing them. The referenced text is the game's title.

name: open_display_with_mode_setup
description: Opens the graphics library through a library vector and, on success, sets display mode values and clears a status byte. On failure it closes the library and returns the error value.

name: open_display_with_mode_setup
description: Opens the graphics library through a library vector and, on success, sets display mode values and clears a status byte. On failure it closes the library and returns the error value.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: A one-instruction fragment decoded from a gap in the code. The pseudo-code shown is the body of a neighbouring routine, so it cannot be read on its own.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: A one-instruction fragment decoded from a gap in the code. The pseudo-code shown is the body of a neighbouring routine, so it cannot be read on its own.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: A one-instruction fragment decoded from a gap in the code. The pseudo-code shown is the body of a neighbouring routine, so it cannot be read on its own.

name: load_popsam_sound_sample
description: Opens the sample file named popsam, allocates memory for its contents and reads it in. It prints a not-enough-memory or cannot-find-file message on failure.

name: clear_status_byte_and_return
description: Clears one status byte in a structure at a fixed offset and returns the stack argument unchanged.

name: free_memory_and_restore_state
description: Restores saved interrupt and display globals, calls a library routine to free memory, and resets the state. It touches the interrupt enable and request registers.

name: dispatch_by_character_code
description: Compares a character argument with two codes and calls one of two unnamed routines for each, then clears a status byte in the structure.

name: clear_status_after_conditional_call
description: Calls an unnamed routine when the character argument equals one, then clears a status byte in the structure.

name: clear_status_byte_and_return
description: Clears one status byte in a structure at a fixed offset and returns the stack argument unchanged.

name: clear_status_byte_and_return
description: Clears one status byte in a structure at a fixed offset and returns the stack argument unchanged.

name: clear_status_byte_and_return
description: Clears one status byte in a structure at a fixed offset and returns the stack argument unchanged.

name: clear_status_byte_and_return
description: Clears one status byte in a structure at a fixed offset and returns the stack argument unchanged.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: A one-instruction fragment decoded from a gap. The pseudo-code runs into a neighbouring table-building routine, so it cannot be read on its own.

name: build_dispatch_tables_from_globals
description: Builds dispatch tables from values in a global variable table, calls two unnamed routines, and ends in a return from exception. It is part of the interrupt setup.

name: clear_state_and_set_defaults
description: Clears a state byte and sets two global words to fifteen and two hundred fifty-five before calling an unnamed routine.

name: start_audio_channel_from_record
description: Selects an audio channel from a table and writes its location, length, period and volume registers from a sample record. It calls three unnamed routines along the way.

name: update_audio_channel_from_samples
description: Copies sample bytes from two sources and updates an audio channel's location and length registers, then sets the DMA control register. It calls two unnamed routines.

name: check_flag_bits_and_signal
description: Tests two bits in a global variable and, when either is set, writes a byte of 255 and stores the masked bits before calling an unnamed routine.

name: write_audio_channel_registers
description: Copies sample bytes between two buffers while updating an audio channel's location, length and period registers. It calls six unnamed routines along the way.

name: update_audio_channel_period
description: Updates an audio channel's period and location registers from a sample pointer and calls one unnamed routine.

name: update_audio_channel_volume
description: Updates an audio channel's location, length and volume registers from a sample record and calls one unnamed routine.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: A one-instruction fragment decoded from a gap in the code. Its pseudo-code is a piece of the audio channel routine next to it, so it cannot be read on its own.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: A three-instruction fragment decoded from a gap in the code. Its pseudo-code is a piece of the audio channel routine next to it, so it cannot be read on its own.

name: copy_sample_bytes_to_buffer
description: Copies bytes from a sample source into a buffer and sets an audio channel's location and period registers. It calls one unnamed routine.

name: enable_audio_dma_for_channel
description: Writes an audio channel's pointer, length and period registers and sets the DMA control register to enable that channel. It calls one unnamed routine.

name: load_audio_sample_for_channel
description: Loads an audio sample for a channel by writing its location, length and period registers, calling four unnamed routines to prepare the data.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: A three-instruction fragment decoded from a gap in the code. Its pseudo-code is a piece of the audio channel routine next to it, so it cannot be read on its own.

name: update_audio_channel_fragment
description: A short fragment that writes audio channel location and length registers from a sample pointer and calls one unnamed routine.

name: update_audio_channel_fragment
description: A short fragment that writes audio channel location and length registers from a sample pointer and calls one unnamed routine.

name: combine_words_with_mask_table
description: Iterates over a block of words, combining each with entries from a global table using bitwise AND, OR and NOT. It updates four spaced locations per pass.

name: mask_destination_words_from_source
description: Loops over source and destination word arrays, masking each destination word with its source word and a global table using AND, NOT and OR. It updates four spaced locations per pass.

name: store_stack_word_and_call
description: Copies a word from the stack into a global variable, calls an unnamed routine, and returns its two input registers unchanged.

name: forward_call_and_return
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns. It adds no logic of its own.

name: read_mouse_movement_deltas
description: Reads the mouse port movement and button state, converting the change since the last sample into clamped signed deltas.

name: split_word_into_byte_globals
description: Stores the low byte and high byte of a global word into two separate globals, then calls an unnamed routine.

name: save_and_enable_interrupt_bits
description: Saves two globals and writes an interrupt enable value with the set bit, then calls nothing further and returns.

name: clear_interrupts_when_flagged
description: If a global flag is set, writes the interrupt clear mask and then the enable value, clears the flag and returns the register value.

name: init_dma_list_structure
description: Initialises a structure from its parameters: zeroes its first word, packs fields into the second, and copies shorts from the source through a loop. It writes DMA control values.

name: wait_for_copper_bit_set
description: Stores a parameter in a global, then loops until bit five of the global is set and returns the combined value. It reads the copper pointer register.

name: spin_until_status_bit_set
description: Writes a constant to a global variable and spins until bit five of that global is set, then returns the bit.

name: copy_shorts_after_marker
description: Searches a short array for the marker value of 384, then copies a count of shorts from a source pointer into the array just after the marker.

name: routine_pseudocode_unavailable
description: Decompiled pseudo-code is unavailable for this routine, so only its layout is known: it is 21 instructions long and called from one place. Its purpose cannot be recovered from the evidence.

name: select_byte_buffer_by_index
description: Looks up a byte buffer pointer from a table using a parameter, then updates a byte in that buffer using bit masks. It is called from one place.

name: decode_keyboard_serial_byte
description: Reads the keyboard serial register and decodes the key code against a character table of digits and symbols, then updates keyboard state globals.

name: copy_eight_thousand_words
description: Copies eight thousand words from a source pointer to a destination pointer, one word per step.

name: copy_words_via_stack_buffer
description: Copies a block of words from a source pointer into a 32-word stack buffer, then processes it in rows while reading the video beam position register. It calls two unnamed routines.

name: call_then_forward_with_result
description: Calls one unnamed routine with no arguments, then calls another with its two parameters and returns that second result.

name: call_then_conditional_follow_up
description: Calls an unnamed routine with its parameter, then calls a second unnamed routine only when a global variable is nonzero.

name: advance_global_return_high_bits
description: Calls an unnamed routine, adds a fixed constant to its result, stores the sum in a global, and returns the high fifteen bits of it.

name: open_dos_library_or_alert
description: Stores the high word of its argument in a global. The gap-decoded body is listed as calling an alert, opening the old dos library and entering supervisor mode, but the pseudo-code shown is incomplete.

name: stub_return_only
description: An empty stub that only returns to its caller and does no work.

name: setup_dos_input_and_directory
description: Allocates a buffer, reads input through the dos library and sets the current directory. It stores the buffer pointer in a global and calls several dos wrapper routines.

name: scan_text_commands_and_dispatch
description: Scans a text buffer character by character and calls one of four unnamed routines for each matched entry. The pseudo-code is large, so the exact command set is not recoverable from it.

name: append_string_with_limit
description: Finds the end of the destination string, then copies characters from the source into it, stopping at the terminator or after a limit of 32766 characters.

name: append_bytes_up_to_count
description: Finds the end of the destination string and appends bytes from the source until a null terminator is reached or the count runs out.

name: copy_string_and_zero_pad
description: Copies bytes from the source to the destination up to a count or until a null terminator, then fills the rest of the count with zeros.

name: multiply_long_pair_to_quad
description: Multiplies two 32-bit values from the registers, building a 64-bit product from the high and low halves of each operand.

name: open_icon_library_and_file
description: Opens a file through the dos library and then the icon library through a library vector, storing the handle in a global. The referenced text is the window name and the icon library.

name: call_optional_handler_then_routine
description: Calls a stored function pointer when it is set, then calls one unnamed routine.

name: call_optional_handler_then_routine
description: Checks a global variable and calls the stored function pointer when it is nonzero, then calls one unnamed routine.
